audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 3, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for dynastic marriage, high places, dream revelation, wisdom, sex-worker access to justice, infant death, maternal testimony, threatened child cutting, and fear of royal judgment.

verses.restored: Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt. He took Pharaoh's daughter and brought her into City of David until he finished building his house, house of YHWH, and wall of Jerusalem around it.
The people were sacrificing at high places, because no house had yet been built for name of YHWH in those days.
Solomon loved YHWH, walking in statutes of David his father; only he sacrificed and burned incense at high places.
The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for it was the great high place. Solomon offered one thousand burnt offerings upon that altar.
At Gibeon YHWH appeared to Solomon in a dream by night. Divine said, Ask what I shall give you.

Solomon said, You showed great covenant-kindness to your servant David my father, as he walked before you in faithfulness, righteousness, and uprightness of heart. You kept for him this great kindness and gave him a son sitting upon his throne this day.
Now, YHWH my Divine, you made your servant king in place of David my father, but I am a small child; I do not know how to go out or come in.
Your servant is in midst of your chosen people, a great people too numerous to count.
Give your servant a listening heart to judge your people, to discern between good and evil, for who can judge this weighty people of yours?
The word was good in eyes of Lord, that Solomon asked this thing.
Divine said to him, Because you asked this and did not ask for long days, riches, or life of your enemies, but asked understanding to hear judgment,
look, I have done according to your word. I have given you a wise and discerning heart, so none like you was before you and none like you shall arise after you.
I have also given what you did not ask—riches and honor—so no king shall be like you all your days.
If you walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and commands as David your father walked, then I will lengthen your days.
Solomon awoke, and look, it was a dream. He came to Jerusalem, stood before ark of covenant of YHWH, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and made a feast for all his servants.
Then two women, sex workers, came to king and stood before him.
One woman said, Please, my lord, I and this woman live in one house, and I gave birth with her in house.
On third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth. We were together; no outsider was with us in house, only we two.
This woman's son died in night because she lay upon him.
She arose in middle of night and took my son from beside me while your maidservant slept. She laid him in her embrace and laid her dead son in my embrace.
I arose in morning to nurse my son, and look, he was dead. But I examined him in morning, and look, it was not my son whom I bore.
The other woman said, No, the living is my son and the dead is your son. The first said, No, the dead is your son and the living is my son. Thus they spoke before king.
The king said, This one says, This is my living son and your son is dead; and that one says, No, your son is dead and my son is living.
The king said, Bring me a sword. They brought sword before king.
The king said, Divide living child in two and give half to one and half to other.

The woman whose son was living spoke to king, for her womb/compassion burned for her son: Please, my lord, give her living child, and killing do not kill him. But the other said, Neither mine nor yours—divide him.
The king answered, Give her living child, and killing do not kill him; she is his mother.
All Israel heard judgment king judged, and they feared king, for they saw wisdom of Divine was within him to do justice.

translation_notes: Pharaoh's daughter enters the story as a diplomatic marriage partner whose consent, name, and political experience are not recorded. International alliance does not make a woman transferable property.
Solomon asks for a listening heart. Wisdom is accountable discernment for people, not brilliance, wealth, certainty, or domination.
The two women are identified by stigmatized labor yet receive direct access to the king. Their occupation does not reduce credibility, motherhood, grief, or legal standing.
The dead infant's death is narrated through accidental overlaying in ancient sleeping conditions. It must not be used to shame bereaved parents or claim certainty about modern infant deaths.
The sword threat is a dangerous judicial performance involving a living child. It should not be copied as interrogation, custody practice, or proof that threats reveal truth.
The compassionate response helps Solomon identify the mother in the narrative, but maternal worth cannot be reduced to self-erasure or willingness to surrender a child.
Israel fears the king after the judgment. Admiration and fear are not identical to safe, transparent, appealable justice.
safety_note: Do not use Solomon's test as a model for threatening children, coercive custody decisions, or traumatizing witnesses. Do not stigmatize sex workers or bereaved parents. A listening heart must center safety, evidence, access, and the least harmful path.
